newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin returns to Kremlin after long gap.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin returns to Kremlin after long gap.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin returned to the Kremlin on Monday, almost exactly seven weeks after undergoing a major operation on his heart.

A Reuters Television crew saw the presidential motorcade arrive at the Kremlin soon after 9.30 a.m. (0630 GMT). Yeltsin had a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 and has been recovering since then in hospital and in government resthomes in the Moscow region and beyond it.
Yeltsin moved to an official residence near Moscow on Sunday ready for his trip back to the Kremlin.
The president, speaking in his first television address since the operation, said on Friday that Russia needed an active president, new ideas and courage, and he promised an energetic return to work.
Yeltsin, 65, looked much thinner than before his surgery and he spoke in a firm and decisive voice.
But he appeared somewhat stiff and distant, lacking the spark which he displayed during his campaign for re-election in the first half of this year.
